prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics and Fluid-Mechanical Machines and Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Students should know, understand and distinguish the different types of maintenance in the industrial field.
Understand failure mechanisms and concepts of device lifespan.
Have knowledge and know maintenance management tools.
Understand maintenance as an integrated part of the industrial company.
Have a criterion for performing an analysis and diagnosis of a maintenance problem.

teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (practical aspects of maintenance techniques, planning, and management, identification of failure mechanisms, description and use of condition-based maintenance techniques like Thermography, Vibrations, Ultrasonics, Magnetic Particles, and Penetrant Liquids, company visit or specialist conference)
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum score equivalent to 40% of the exam value (2.8 out of 7 points) is required on the final theoretical-practical exam. If this minimum is not reached, the course will not be passed, and a grade of 4.9 will be recorded. Attendance at laboratory practices is mandatory for evaluation. For the extraordinary call and differentiated evaluation, the final exam covers theory and classroom practices (80%), and laboratory practice content (20%). A minimum of 5 out of 10 points is required to pass the course in any call.
